event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing, dated four years after the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic, treats the pandemic primarily as an ongoing but now better-understood operational and financial exposure rather than as an acute crisis. The text shows that the company continues to feel medium-term effects: (i) lingering uncertainty around in-person conferences, (ii) unresolved, high-dollar litigation over event-cancellation insurance for 2020–2021, (iii) an explicit loss of insurance protection for any future disease-related cancellations, and (iv) structural changes such as a hybrid workforce that increases cyber-security risk. These statements are specific—naming COVID-19, dollar limits (up to $170 m and $150 m) and concrete business processes—yet mostly forward-looking or contingent (“could,” “has contested,” “excludes”). Under the Time Decay Principle, the event is four years old, so maximum individual evidence scores should fall in the moderate 4-6 band. Overall, the disclosures reflect a material, continuing risk that is being partially mitigated by prior insurance recoveries and operational adaptations, justifying a moderate aggregate severity assessment.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, because our conferences are scheduled in advance and held at specific locations, the success of these activities can be affected by circumstances outside of our control, such as the occurrence of or concerns related to communicable diseases (such as COVID-19), labor strikes, transportation shutdowns and travel restrictions, economic slowdowns, reductions in government spending, geopolitical crises, terrorist attacks, war, weather, natural disasters, and other occurrences impacting the global, regional, or national economies, the occurrence of any of which could negatively impact the success of the conference or meeting.

Describes potential negative operational impact (loss of conference success) in forward-looking terms.

evidence_list.snippet: This insurance included coverage for cancellations due to communicable diseases and enabled us to receive an amount up to the lost contribution margin per conference plus incurred expenses, as more specifically set forth in the policies’ provisions for calculating the amount of recoverable loss, and subject to the policies’ limits of liability.
